thread_text:
Aisha (PM): quick sync — dropping a short infra lifecycle proposal for the routing/policy + multi-region isolation work. trying to balance customer-driven asks (residency, cutover windows) with SLO/cost constraints. please react with major objections.

Raj (Staff Architect): high level looks sane. couple notes: model-aware routing needs explicit compatibility matrix, and fallback chains must be first-class. we can't assume KV-cache compatibility across quantized variants.

Mei (SRE): agree with Raj. launch criteria we should require: 99.9% p95 token latency for canary tenants, end-to-end synthetic smoke for 24h, and automated rollback on error rate spike >3x baseline. also need runbook template.

Lina (Infra Eng): capacity gating callout: every tenant cutover must run a dry-run traffic profile against reserved capacity; autoscale policies need a pre-provisioned buffer (configurable). we should include an "eviction window" policy for noisy tenants.

Tomas (AE): from customers — residency + maintenance windows are the big asks. they want predictable cutover weeks (not midnight surprises) and a contract clause for rollback. can we scope an opt-in scheduled migration path?

Ken (ML Eng): routing must be model-aware: prefer lighter quantized variants for latency-sensitive lanes but keep a quality regression check. propose a simple routing weight file per tenant. also we need to capture prompt/length distributions pre-cutover.

Aisha (PM): proposed phased plan (short):
1) Q3 pilot: policy-DSL v0 (read-only) + 3 pilot tenants (opt-in).
2) Q3->Q4: policy-DSL v1 (enforceable) + canary rollouts, dedicated buffer config.
3) Q4: full migration API + contract/onboarding checklist.

Aisha (PM): minimal launch criteria list (for product signoff):
- successful 24h canary for 3 tenants with latency and error SLOs met
- runbook + rollback tested in staging (playbook run)
- capacity gating validated (dry-run traffic)
- customer communication template + agreed migration windows

Raj (Staff Architect): technical acceptance checklist additions:
- policy translation tests (DSL -> runtime) pass for all model variants
- fallback policy precedence defined (region -> model family -> quantization)
- telemetry hooks (per-request routing decision + reason)

Mei (SRE): runbook sketch (inline):
```
1) Verify canary tenant metrics baseline (last 7d)
2) Enable policy-DSL v1 for canary at 10% traffic
3) Monitor RPS, p95, model failure rates, and tail errors
4) If error rate > 3x or p95 regresses > 30%, roll back and tag incident
```

Lina (Infra Eng): autoscale knobs to expose in config:
- buffer_percent (default 20%)
- max_burst_instances
- preprovision_window_minutes

Tomas (AE): question — for enterprise customers who require ironclad residency, can we offer a 'migration concierge' (SE + infra lead) as an add-on? will ease adoption.

Aisha (PM): yes, add to sales ops playbook. also propose a canary incentives program (reduced price for pilot months).

Ken (ML Eng): telemetry notes — we should store a small labeled prompt set per tenant for quality regression checks post-migration. flag any embeddings/semantic drift.

Raj (Staff Architect): one more: ops must be able to pin fallback to a known-good model variant by tenant via the DSL. emergency API should exist.

Mei (SRE): tagging for postmortem: action_owner, rollout_id, tenant_id. that's critical for RCA.

Aisha (PM): next steps:
- Raj/Lina: draft policy-DSL v1 minimal grammar by EOW
- Mei: draft runbook template + automated smoke tests by next Wed
- Tomas: pick 3 pilot tenants and confirm dates by EOD Monday
- Ken: propose telemetry dataset shape for regression checks by Tue

deploy-bot: created a doc: https://redwood/team/doc/infra-lifecycle-cutover-proposal (permissions: product, infra, sre) :white_check_mark:

Lina (Infra Eng): noted the action items. I'll schedule a 30m tech deep-dive Wed 10:00 to finalize DSL tradeoffs.

Aisha (PM): thanks all — please drop short replies if you can take the action or if timeline is impossible. :thumbsup:
